title: Charts from a file
summary: Real numbers live in files, not in your code. pandas reads a CSV file into a table in one line, df["Column"] picks a column, and a column goes straight into plt.bar() or plt.plot(). Change the file and the chart follows.
objectives: Read a CSV file into a table with pd.read_csv().
Explain why charts should read their numbers from the file.

slides.h: By the end: the chart follows the file
slides.say: weather.csv holds Sundarpur’s year: one row per month with its rain, average temperature and sunny days. Read it with pandas, then chart any column. Next year, swap the file and run it again.
points: `import pandas as pd` loads pandas, the library for tables.
`df = pd.read_csv("weather.csv")` reads the whole file into a table (a DataFrame).
p: weather.csv holds Sundarpur’s year: one row per month with its rain, average temperature and sunny days. Read it with pandas, then chart any column. Next year, swap the file and run it again.
`import pandas as pd` loads pandas, the library for tables.
`df = pd.read_csv("weather.csv")` reads the whole file into a table (a DataFrame).

slides.say: A column works wherever a list did. `plt.bar(df["Month"], df["Rain_mm"])` draws the same bars as typed lists, but now from the file.
points: Column names are exact, capitals and underscores included: "Rain_mm".
The rows’ order is the bars’ order.
p: A column works wherever a list did. `plt.bar(df["Month"], df["Rain_mm"])` draws the same bars as typed lists, but now from the file.

slides.say: Numbers typed into code are right once. When the city publishes next year’s figures, the code still draws last year. Read them from the file and the same program draws any year, any city.
points: Sheetah’s hidden tests use other cities’ files, so typed-in numbers fail them.
Your program is a recipe; the file is the ingredients.

points: A KeyError’s message is the name it couldn’t find.

bank.q: Why read the numbers from the file rather than typing them?
options: The same program then charts any year or any city

bank.q: How do you see a file’s exact column names?

points: `df = pd.read_csv("file.csv")` reads a table; `df["Col"]` is one column.
A column goes into `plt.bar` or `plt.plot` just like a list.
Read numbers from the file so the chart works for any file.

cards.front: Why not type the numbers in?
cards.back: Then the chart is right for one file only; reading the file works for any.
